items.title: labs(reliability): fresh user per recall trial — report the true recall rate
items.body:
## What

The reliability gate's recall assertions reused ONE run-user across all trials, each storing a *different* `locker code` / sister-name fact. So the user's memory store accumulated conflicting same-type facts and the brain had to pick the exact newest — an artificial pileup that measured conflict-resolution, not recall. It under-reported recall as a blanket ~20%.

## Fix

The two recall assertions now provision a **fresh user per trial** (empty store — what a real user actually has). The deterministic assertions (identity/research/write) keep the shared user; they don't accumulate conflicting facts.

## Result (with `ZOE_SEAM_RECALL_INJECT` on, extract-wait 45s)

| assertion | before (contaminated) | after (fresh per trial) |
|---|---|---|
| `recall_just_stored` | 20% | **100%** (3/3) |
| `corrected_recall` | 0–20% | 33% — a real 4B correction-precedence weakness, no longer masked |

Independently corroborated: a fresh-user-per-trial manual run hit **8/8** on single-fact cross-session recall. The flag flip took recall from ~20% to ~100%; this makes the gate *report* that truth instead of its own contamination.

`corrected_recall` at 33% is now honestly surfaced as the remaining recall weakness (recency ordering #1124 helps but the 4B still waffles Katie/Kate) — a candidate for the next fix, not a gate artifact.

LAB-only; no `services/zoe-data` changes.

items.title: labs(reliability): statistical reliability gate for the live flue brain
items.body:
## What

`labs/flue-zoe-brain/parity/reliability_gate.py` — a **statistical** reliability gate for the live flue brain. Single-pass parity gates hide 4B-model variance: a prompt can pass one round and fail the next *identically phrased* (the persona leak in `FIX-PACKET-2026-07-07.md` item 2 was 1-in-30; corrected-recall Kate-not-Katie is model judgment). This mirrors the rigor that proved `recall_memory` at ~97% over ≥30 trials (`recall_reliability.py` / `RELIABILITY.md`).

## How

Runs **each** of five highest-value, historically-flaky assertions N times (`--trials`, default 10) and gates on a per-assertion pass **RATE**, not a single pass:

| Assertion | Kind | Verify | Threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| recall of a just-stored fact | recall | substring | ≥ 90% |
| corrected recall (Kate not Katie) | recall | substring | ≥ 90% |
| identity: name = Zoe (never Gemma) | deterministic | substring | 100% |
| research-trap statement no stall | deterministic | substring | 100% |
| DB-verified shopping-list write | deterministic | Postgres | 100% |

- Drives the **live authenticated `/api/chat/?stream=false`** (routes to flue via `ZOE_BRAIN_BACKEND=flue`) — the surface production uses, so it's a whole-pipeline read.
- **Fresh authenticated test user provisioned per run** (`provision_parity_test_user.py` → login for `X-Session-ID`) → empty memory store per run.
- **Every trial uses a fresh nonce'd conversation `session_id`** — mirrors `hard_gate.py`; sessions are ownership-bound and long ones overflow the brain at 8192 tokens.
- **Auto-verified, no human in the pass/fail path**: recall/identity/research by substring, writes against Postgres `list_items` ground truth (said == did — a reply that claims it wrote but didn't FAILs).
- Thresholds override with `--threshold-recall` / `--threshold-deterministic`.

## Scope

Lab-only; **no `services/zoe-data` changes**. Runtime result lands in the gitignored `reliability_gate_last.json`. `RELIABILITY.md` documents the gate.

## Smoke (`--trials 2`, live)

Exit 0, valid per-assertion output. The 3 deterministic assertions passed 100% (identity → "My name is Zoe…", research statement drew a follow-up not a research stall, both DB writes verified present). The 2 recall assertions each split 1/2 at N=2 — **exactly the variance this gate exists to surface** (corrected-recall waffled "name is Katie, and you prefer to be called Kate" on one trial; recall bled a prior trial's nonce on another). A 2-trial smoke can't clear a ≥90% threshold and isn't meant to — it proves the harness runs.

**Full N=10 sweep is deferred: the shared brain is mid-campaign.** Run it post-round-3, in a quiet GPU window, sequential (one shared GPU).

items.title: docs(bench): measure TTT checkpoint impact vs untrained baseline
items.body:
## Summary

First measurement of the model-dependent half of Axiom (absorption, drift detection, recall, compression) against the real trained checkpoint present on this machine (`checkpoints/axiom_production_bpe.bin`), rather than the `ln(vocab)` entropy floor every prior audit (June, July, 2026-08-08) hit because `checkpoints/` is gitignored and never shipped.

Full writeup: `bench/ttt/RESULTS-2026-08-09.md`

## Findings

- **Absorption: real signal.** `CE 7.494 -> 7.402` with the checkpoint vs `5.545 -> 5.545` (= `ln(256)` exactly) untrained. Works as designed.
- **Drift detection: does not discriminate, even with the checkpoint.** Clean and deliberately anomalous code both score `CE = 8.9872` (= `ln(8000)` exactly) with the checkpoint loaded — the 7.03 threshold can't separate them, it just always fires. Without a checkpoint, drift is reported `UNAVAILABLE`. This is a previously-unknown bug — having a checkpoint doesn't fix it.
- **Recall: never actually measurable.** `eval_recall`'s embedder expects a `[256]`-shaped `ln_f.weight` (legacy tokenizer architecture); the production BPE checkpoint is `[128]`-shaped. The load fails and it silently falls back to a random model in *both* configs — the identical precision@k numbers are not evidence checkpoints don't help recall, they're evidence the tool never loaded one.
- **Compression: partially model-independent.** Structural skeleton extraction is identical both ways (2229/2229 signature round-trip, 100%), confirming the core extraction logic is model-independent. But raw/skeleton token *counts* differ ~3x because `AXIOM_PRODUCTION_BPE` also switches the active tokenizer — the headline "82.4% compression" figure is tokenizer-dependent, not fixed.

## Test plan

- [x] Ran each measurement twice (with checkpoint / `AXIOM_PRODUCTION_BPE=0`), captured raw output
- [x] Checkpoint provenance recorded (vocab_size, val_ce, training source/date)
- [x] No tuning, no default changes — measurement only, per task constraints
- [ ] Follow-up: investigate why `axiom_evaluate_drift`'s CE doesn't reflect the loaded checkpoint the way `self_heal.rs`'s absorption path does
- [ ] Follow-up: fix `eval_recall`'s embedder to accept the BPE checkpoint shape, or document that a separate `axiom_embedder.bin` is required

items.title: Close the adaptivity loop: relearning, review-aware lessons, remediat…
items.body:
…ion, visible mastery

The review phase, lesson, and mastery gate were silos — a student could fail most of review and the lesson would teach new material minutes later as if nothing happened, with the only consequence (the week not advancing) invisible until days later.

- In-session relearning: a missed or skipped review item is requeued at the end of the current queue (once, labelled 'Second look') so the phase ends on corrected recall. Relearn repeats don't touch SRS schedules, accuracy, or the mastery gate — first attempts only.
- Review-aware lessons: SessionContext now carries today's first-attempt review accuracy and summaries of exactly what was missed. The tutor must treat misses as the top teaching priority; below 70% it front- loads re-teaching, and below 50% the entire lesson becomes remediation.
- Remediation pauses intake: below 50% accuracy the new-vocabulary batch is suppressed. Batching is now driven by the persisted isIntroduced flag instead of session-count arithmetic, so a paused batch simply surfaces next session instead of being skipped forever.
- Visible mastery: the Home week card now shows retention vs the 70% bar alongside session count, and explains when the next session will run as consolidation. Session notes record misses so the next session's tutor sees them too.
- Skill scores and the stored session record use first-attempt counts, keeping the mastery gate honest.

items.title: docs: rebuild the README to the reader ladder, correct three claims, and close the sdist
items.body:
An audit of this repository's documentation against the portfolio house style, followed by the fixes it turned up. Three commits, each independently reviewable.

## What the audit found

The README was close to exactly ladder-inverted. Nothing on the first screen told a non-specialist what this is; the project's best material — that it audited its own evaluation, found the scorer counting training-period events as missed detections, and corrected recall from `0.24` to `0.42` — sat at word ~400 as the second bullet of a four-bullet list. "Does it work, show me" arrived at word ~1,710 and "how do I start" at ~1,748, in a 2,266-word page mixing explanation, reference and how-to.

Twenty-one unglossed field terms appeared in the first three paragraphs.

## What changed

**`docs`** — the finding now leads, and it is earned rather than asserted: the question first (is the model weak, or is the scoring wrong?), then the answer, then the before/after. Status moved into a blockquote near the top. Nothing was deleted; everything over a paragraph that is not a ladder rung moved to a linked document — `docs/datasets.md` for provenance and claim scope, `docs/engineering_envelope.md` for the evidence table, architecture and local stack, `CONTRIBUTING.md` for tooling posture. 2,266 → 1,007 words. The licence badge now links to the licence file. Every relative link resolves.

Three claims corrected in the same commit:

- `public_results.md` said `658x` where `claims.md` and the README said `657x`. `166570.542613 / 253.465322 = 657.2`.
- `claims.md` D3 said applying the full ESA-ADB metric hierarchy was upstream work in telemeval. telemeval now ships ADTQC and channel/subsystem-aware F-beta, so the remaining gap is local. The old reason is recorded, not overwritten.
- Nothing here disclosed that telemeval's event-wise *precision* uses its own run-based definition, diverging from ESA-ADB's TNR-corrected `EW_*`, while *recall* matches exactly. telemeval documents this; this repository did not. Now both do.

Two counts were removed rather than updated — the pinned test total and the repo-wide mypy error figure. A count that routine work changes cannot be kept true on a surface you no longer control.

**`chore(lint)`** — Google docstring convention recorded in `pyproject.toml`, with ruff `D2`/`D4` selected and `D1` deliberately not. `D4` was already clean; `D2` reported 360 `D202`, all whitespace and all auto-fixable. Every module already carries a module docstring, so there was no coverage to chase.

**`fix(packaging)`** — the sdist had no file selection, so hatchling packaged the working tree minus the *repository's* `.gitignore`. Building it and opening it showed `.claude/settings.local.json`, carrying absolute machine paths, and the whole `graphify-out/` cache. Nothing publishes this package, so nothing leaked — the point is that no source-tree check could see it. Now an allowlist, which fails closed, with a test pinning that every entry matches something git tracks.

## Verification

`ruff`, the scoped `mypy` gate, and the full suite are green locally — 465 passed, 0 skipped. The sdist fix was verified by rebuilding the artifact and opening it (339 → 191 files, no `.claude`, no `graphify-out`), not by reading the source tree. The enforcing test was verified by sabotage: an empty list, a local-only entry and an untracked entry are each rejected by the assertion meant to catch them.

Two README commands were not run: `docker compose up --build` and the demo-image build. The Docker daemon was not available; `docker compose config` parses clean. Everything else in the README was executed.

## Not in scope

The project's future is being decided separately. Nothing here archives, deprecates, or adds a roadmap.

items.title: docs: the hard fixture set changes retrieval.md's conclusion
items.body:
Follow-up to #161. That PR built the instrument; this one reports what it measured, in the document that had been claiming the opposite.

`docs/retrieval.md` said the matcher was **saturated** — recall@3 of 1.000, no headroom, further tuning not worth doing. Against the 70-fixture hard set: **recall@1 0.442, recall@3 0.481.**

## The finding is the per-class split, not the drop

| Class | recall@1 | recall@3 | mean overlap |
|---|---|---|---|
| near-dup | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.783 |
| user-voice | 0.200 | 0.333 | 0.229 |
| paraphrase | **0.000** | **0.000** | 0.000 |

BM25 is *perfect* on the class deliberately built to be hard — telling genuinely near-duplicate tools apart — and scores zero on seventeen paraphrases sharing no vocabulary with their target:

> "everywhere this identifier appears, swap in a new label instead" → **nothing returned**. The tool is `rider:rename_refactoring`, whose document says "rename", "refactoring", "symbol".

That is not a ranking failure and no weight sweep or threshold change can reach it — the terms are not in the corpus. It moves the open question from scoring to vocabulary.

The honest summary, now in the document: the first fixture set was measuring the matcher's strongest case and reporting it as the whole picture. The saturation was real; the conclusion drawn from it was an artefact of the instrument.

## Also corrected

- **recall@1 0.907 → 0.930** on the easy set, no matcher change — #161 repaired a fixture naming one of two functionally identical tools and scoring the other as wrong.
- **The two "margins" are disambiguated.** Threshold headroom (0.0089) and the runner's class separation `coverage_margin` (−0.201) measure different things and disagree in sign. Both correct; readers seeing both without explanation would reasonably conclude one was a bug.
- The regression gate and the instrument are now described as different things — the hard set asserts no recall bar on purpose, because a gate you can always pass tells you only that you have not regressed.

## Deliberately not changed

The 0.48.0 changelog entry still reports recall@1 of 0.907. That is what 0.48.0 shipped with. A changelog entry records a tree at a point in time; editing it to match a later measurement falsifies the record rather than correcting it.

Verified: `docs_guard` PASS (126 documents), all three mermaid diagrams re-parsed against mermaid 11, every number reproduced by running `tooling/retrieval_eval.py` on both sets and recomputing both Wilson intervals.

items.title: Operating-point PR-curve + AP analysis, with GT-completeness check (#54)
items.body:
## What

Implements #54 — characterize RampNet's detection operating point properly: a continuous PR curve + honest AP, and a ground-truth-completeness correction (#55).

`scripts/analysis/operating_point_curve.py`, three subcommands:
- **extract** (GPU, once): inference per pano, extract every peak down to a low score floor (default 0.05, `min_distance=10`), peak height = confidence → portable per-pano JSON cache.
- **curve** (CPU): re-threshold the cache post-hoc → PR curve, **AP** (extract-once-at-floor fixes the committed bundle's 0.5-peak AP truncation so it's comparable), F1-vs-threshold; CSVs + PNGs with deployed-0.55 and F1-optimum marked.
- **gallery** (CPU): render the *incremental* FPs (unmatched preds with score in `[op, 0.55)`) as native-pano crops into a self-contained A/B/unsure-tagging `index.html`; `--tags` → corrected precision, recall and F1 with an error band.

## Results (richmond + bend)

| city | AP | deployed 0.55 | F1-optimal (raw) |
|---|---|---|---|
| richmond | 0.876 | P .964 / R .768 / F1 .855 | thr 0.35: P .921 / R .823 / F1 .869 |
| bend | 0.868 | P .980 / R .755 / F1 .853 | thr 0.50: P .981 / R .786 / F1 .873 |

`(0.55, 10)` reproduces the committed benchmark P/R exactly → pipeline validated.

### GT-completeness correction (#55) — both cities reviewed

All 53 incremental FPs were tagged by hand (5 unsure). Corrected numbers:

| city | thr | raw P/R/F1 | **corrected P/R/F1** |
|---|---|---|---|
| richmond | 0.25 | .872 / .839 / .855 | **.889 / .841 / .865** |
| richmond | 0.30 | .902 / .829 / .864 | **.919 / .832 / .873** |
| richmond | 0.35 | .921 / .823 / .869 | **.928 / .824 / .873** |
| bend | 0.25 | .904 / .835 / .868 | **.927 / .838 / .881** |
| bend | 0.30 | .924 / .823 / .871 | **.942 / .825 / .880** |
| bend | 0.35 | .929 / .804 / .862 | **.943 / .807 / .870** |

**The correction moves the F1 optimum down** — richmond 0.35 → 0.30, bend 0.50 → 0.25/0.30 — because the low-confidence band was being penalised for surfacing ramps the GT never had. That is the result #55 was built to test.

**A-rate: richmond 17% (5/29), bend 29% (7/24).** A quarter of bend's low-confidence "false positives" are real unlabelled ramps. Tags are committed at `benchmark/<city>/incremental_fp_tags.json`, so `gallery --tags` reproduces every number here.

**No operating point is recommended yet.** Only 2 of 5 benchmark cities have been corrected; clovis, morgantown and manual_gold have not. The A-rate differs by 12 points between the two cities measured, so it is not yet a constant anyone should extrapolate. The deployment constant handed to `sidewalk-auto-labeler` should wait for the remaining splits.

## Three defects found and fixed while doing the review

These changed the answer, not just the ergonomics:

1. **Duplicates were indistinguishable from discoveries.** `greedy_match` already returns `saw_in_range` — a GT ramp *inside* the match radius that a higher-confidence prediction had claimed — and `classify_predictions` discarded it. So a second hit on one ramp looked exactly like a ramp the GT missed. Now carried through as `redundant`, with distance-to-nearest-GT in radius units and a `duplicate_risk` bucket. **9 of 53 incremental FPs are human-confirmed double-counts.**
2. **The crop was too small to show the evidence.** At `crop_frac 0.08` the frame reached only ±1.8 R, while duplicates live at 1–3 R — so the proof that a detection was a duplicate was cropped out of the image used to judge it. Default is now 0.15 (±3.4 R), and each crop draws the match radius the scorer actually used.
3. **Crops were upscaled mush.** The decode was pinned at 2048 px regardless of crop size, so a bend crop was **163 real pixels** blown up to 512. Decode width is now derived from `crop_frac`/`--render-px`.

An unreviewed first pass made under all three defects put bend at 0/24 and picked richmond A's that the wider crop later refuted — the opposite conclusion on bend. The numbers above are from the corrected tool.

## Also

- **Corrected recall**, not just precision. An A is a ramp the GT lacked, so it adds to recall's numerator *and* denominator; correcting precision alone reported a corrected P against an uncorrected R. Only recall-confirmed panos contribute, so an A on an unscanned pano moves precision but not recall.
- **"Unsure" tagging**, which makes the band mean something: low end credits confirmed As, high end also credits unsure and untagged. Previously both ends were fixed regardless of the tags.
- An **A on a duplicate-risk item is reported, not silently credited** — it caught a real mistake during the bend review.
- Gallery UX: click-to-zoom, keyboard tagging, hide-tagged, tags load as well as export, best-effort autosave (`localStorage` on `file://` is refused by some browsers, so the download stays the real save).
- `docs/model_comparison.md`: the measured A-rate now backs the "RampNet-anchored GT" caveat, with the limit stated — it bounds GT incompleteness, not any challenger's penalty.

## Tests / hygiene
- `tests/test_operating_point_curve.py` — 15 passing. The load-bearing invariant is unchanged: `classify_predictions` reproduces `score_pano`'s tp/fp/ignored exactly over 300 random cases, so the gallery audits the same FPs the curve counts.
- Scoring core reuses `rampnet.detection_eval` / `rampnet.metrics` — no divergent matcher.
- `pyproject.toml`: scope pytest to `tests/` — bare `pytest` was breaking collection on `scripts/analysis/overlap_test.py`. Analysis README refreshed.

## Follow-up

Peak extraction's `min_distance=10` is under half the matcher's 22.5 px radius, so it can emit two peaks inside one ramp's match radius by construction — filed separately, since it changes the deployed extraction path rather than the benchmark correction.

items.title: fix(imagescan): the attacker chooses the line breaks — restore channel fidelity before scanning
items.body:
`main` is red on `tests/test_ocr_recall_corpus.py`. Chasing it found something much larger
than the three failures.

### The finding

`sanitize` treats `\n` as a hard sentence terminator. **On the pixel channel the attacker
chooses where the line breaks fall — because the attacker chooses the image width.** One
break placed inside a rule's gap bypassed `secret_exfil`, `prompt_injection`'s forget arm,
and `fund_routing`.

Measured against #330's own attack set:

| | attack/width pairs caught | attacks surviving every width |
|---|---|---|
| raw pixel channel | **37/68** | 3/17 |
| after `gecko.ocrnorm` | **68/68** | 17/17 |

Address shattering is the second half: OCR reproduces the `0x de ad be ef … remove the
spaces` evasion **by accident, on every image containing an address**.

### The invariant that decided the design

> The pixel channel must reproduce the clean-channel verdict — never looser, never stricter.

Two candidates failed it, and the 2×2 measurement corrected the author:

- **Too loose** — no table guard fused a benign ID table's three cells into a 37-char
  pseudo-address and quarantined the document.
- **Too strict** — refusing to re-join any line of identifiers looked safest and cost
  **18 of 68** pairs, because every short `verb → to → <address>` payload loses its
  address to the wrap at some width. This was chosen first, and was wrong.

Shipped: one identifier on a line is a wrapped sentence and is re-joined; two or more is a
table and is not.

**A false positive introduced and caught by red-teaming, not by a test:** two legitimate
mints side by side — *"The supported mints are So1111…112 J1toso…CPn today."* — fused to 87
chars, tripping the Solana-secret-key matcher and quarantining a benign surface. Fixed by
capping the fuse at 44 chars (one address). The cap *stops* the run rather than abandoning
it — abandoning would make appending a short base58 word a one-token evasion.

**Zero new false positives** across 6,075 committed spec prose fields × 4 wrap widths
(24,300 variants), the curated benign payment/wallet corpus, and the committed benign
fixtures.

### Residuals, moved not deleted

`atk_fund_routing_balance` reads perfectly through pixels — it is not an OCR failure at
all. Moved to `EXPECTED_RESIDUALS` with the reasoning, the 4-in-1,900 measurement, and a
pointer to the #330 trade. `atk_twocol` is now caught *incidentally*; its test asserts the
phrase it was built around is still shredded, so nobody cites it as column-split coverage.

**Corrected recall: 14/18, four named residuals, zero FPs** — stated as *engine plus
normalisation*, because two catches need both and quoting it as a tesseract number would
overstate the engine.

### Does #330 still stand?

**Yes, but its evidence was incomplete.** The trade is unaffected. What changes is the
safety argument: #330 justified removing the bare branch by widening the literal-address
branch — and that branch did not work on the pixel channel **at all** (37/68). The
conclusion holds; the measurement behind it did not cover the channel that matters most
for GhostCommit.

### The lesson as tests

`tests/test_ocrnorm.py` is pure-function and needs no OCR engine, so it runs on the base CI
install where the corpus skips: raw-channel bypasses still bypass, the invariant,
monotonicity, idempotence, linearity. The corpus now asserts the **channel** — fixtures
that must fail raw and pass normalised, plus the FP that undoing it would cause.

**Evasions left open and pinned as executable cases** (`test_evasions_that_remain_open`):
a period or colon before the break, a blank line, two-space gaps, one-character fragments.
Each closure trades a false positive in a BEST-EFFORT channel. This restores fidelity
against a *renderer*; it is not a boundary against someone who has read the module.

items.title: Apply enhanced-review findings to epic_28 (Agent Memory Part 1) stories
items.body:
Applies the enhanced-review findings to the epic_28 (Agent Memory Part 1) story specs. Docs-only.

## Review method
Three independent lenses (analyst / architect / adversarial), each verifying findings against the **live loopctl code**, not just prose. All confirmed findings applied — no deferrals.

## Blockers fixed
- **Removed the human-auth Memory-Inspector LiveView.** Verified: loopctl has zero `on_mount`, no `users`/accounts, no session login, no `fixture(:user)`/`fixture(:tenant_user)` — it is agent-native (API-key only). No web UI is planned for loopctl. Operator visibility+delete is now a **superadmin-gated API path** (US-28.3 AC-28.3.4).
- **Pinned `subject_id` derivation** (US-28.1 AC-28.1.4). `api_key.agent_id` is nullable and `agent` is the *floor* role, so the old "role ≥ agent" gate would have leaked or failed. `subject_id` = `agent_id` for agent keys, else `api_key.id`; never null, never client-supplied.
- **Corrected recall isolation** (US-28.2). Recall runs on `HeavyReadRepo` (**BYPASSRLS**), so isolation is an explicit `(tenant_id, subject_id)` predicate enforced by a **structural guard**, not RLS. Added index-safe subject filtering (over-fetch + post-filter with a scale/EXPLAIN gate) to avoid HNSW under-fill silently starving an agent's own recall.

## Majors fixed
Session read path (`session_history/2`), session TTL + prune worker, `superseded_by on_delete: :nilify_all`, and the previously-untested ACs: pagination/total_count, worker idempotency + Oban `unique`, MCP witness self-heal, recall-supersede exclusion, and **API-level cross-subject isolation** (AC-28.6.4 promised it, no test exercised it).

## Minors fixed
Flat `Loopctl.Workers.*` namespace; OpenAPI operations declared in the controller (schemas in `api_spec/`); role-gate intent documented; write quota/rate-limit; PII/embedding-boundary stance; observable isolation assertions.

## Structure
Terminal story renumbered 28.6 → 28.5 (5 contiguous stories). README documents the review changes and the security model.

Refs #307.

items.title: L2 retrieval funnel: reranker tuning, spell-correction, and smart corpus routing
items.body:
## Summary

This branch hardens the retrieval funnel end-to-end and adds temporal/content-type routing for corpus-wide queries. Work spans four themes:

### L1/L2 funnel tuning
- First-class L1 **pool Recall@K** ablation arm; fixed a pool-truncation bug that made `limit>50` silently return a shallower pool.
- Diagnosis corrected: Recall@50 is 87-90% while reranked HR@5 is 57-77%, so the **MiniLM cross-encoder was the bottleneck, not L1 recall**.
- bge asymmetric query instruction (vector leg); `[Title>Section]` header kept out of the chunk embedding (in FTS only).
- Default reranker -> **MiniLM-L-12, pure CE** (blend was compensating for a weak L-6 CE). Fixed a score-inversion bug where negative CE logits let context-expansion neighbours outrank reranked hits.

### Corpus-wide typo routing
- Norvig edit-distance-1 **query spell-correction** against corpus vocab (`QUERY_SPELL_CORRECT`, default on). Recovers typo-induced routing loss ("Itaca" -> the_odyssey) with zero clean regression.

### Smart corpus routing (temporal + content-type)
- Per-chunk **content-date extraction** (`chunks.entry_date`) with a density gate so a stray reference date in a book doesn't smear across every chunk.
- `parse_query_filters` (pure regex/keyword, no LLM) extracts content-type + a date window; `retrieve()` / `/search` / chat `search_node` filter on `entry_date` and route content-types to document IDs.
- "Generate a story from my daily thoughts notes this month" now routes to the notes doc and returns only that month's entries. Validated live: all 12 July chunks, zero cross-month leakage.
- Fixed the gpt-5 `temperature=0` blank-screen chat crash (`litellm.drop_params`).

### Evals + goldens
- Corpus-wide document-routing eval (`run_corpus_routing.py`), persisted as `eval_kind=corpus_routing` and rendered in the Quality Runs tab.
- Modernized/regenerated corpus-QA and legacy book goldens (gpt-5.4 + cross-verify); generator hardened against sampling Project-Gutenberg boilerplate.
- Parser fix: short transcripts are now turn-grouped instead of collapsing to "(Empty Section)".

## Test plan
- `make ci` green (ablation arm assertions updated for the pure-CE arm).
- New unit tests: `test_content_dates.py`, `test_query_understanding.py`, `test_context_header_fts.py`, rerank-blend guards.
- Smart-routing path validated live end-to-end against an ingested notes journal fixture.

items.title: Phase 4: the ~0.45 recall ceiling is mostly the eval set, not the imagery
items.body:
## The headline

The documented **~0.45 recall ceiling is substantially an artifact of the eval set's box geometry, not a limit of the imagery.** The detector is finding the batteries. The belt-lighting recommendation is **withdrawn pending a re-labeled eval set**, and no recall number from this project should be quoted until that relabeling happens.

`docs/recall_ceiling_findings.md` keeps all its experiments — they reproduce — but now carries a superseded banner over its conclusions. Full writeup: `docs/recall_ceiling_round2.md`.

## Evidence (four independent legs)

**1. Only 5.9% of ground truth is actually undetected.** Of 186 GT boxes: 48.9% covered, **32.8% near-miss (IoU 0.3-0.5)**, 12.4% partial, **5.9% total miss (IoU<0.1)**. Recall would be 0.817 if near-misses alone cleared the bar.

**2. The metric is extraordinarily threshold-sensitive.** Recall 0.452 @IoU0.5 → **0.790 @IoU0.3**. The convention-free question — did a detection land *inside* the GT box — answers **0.839**. Every class shows a 15-48 point gap.

**3. Blind audit: the GT box is the wrong one.** Three auditors judged 36 near-miss panels without being told which box source was which. **34/36 favoured the detector's box** (91.7% unanimous, sign-test p≈2e-9). Visibility: **96 "obvious" / 12 "subtle" / 0 "invisible"** out of 108 ratings. All 30 `ni_mh_all` ratings were "obvious" — the class the old doc calls "essentially invisible (<=0.08 everywhere)".

**4. Contrast is ANTI-correlated with recall.** Measured inside tight detector boxes on raw frames: `ni_cd_small` 10.7 sigma and `ni_mh_all` 6.6 sigma (highest contrast) have the worst recall; `ni_cd_bulk` 2.1 sigma and `li_ion_laptop` 3.2 sigma (lowest) have the best. If darkness caused the ceiling this would run the other way.

## What this deliberately does NOT claim

- No corrected recall number — nobody re-drew a box, so any restated figure would be fabricated.
- Not "the GT is globally bad" — only the disputed band was audited; the 91 boxes already at IoU>=0.5 were never examined.
- Not "lighting is irrelevant" — the audit is structurally blind to the 11 total misses (no detector box means no panel to judge), and that population is exactly where "too dark" could still be true. The supported claim is narrower: lighting cannot explain the *bulk* of the gap, so it is not justified as the *primary* fix.
- Not a diagnosed GT mechanism — "translated down-left, square-aspect-biased" is a visual impression, not a measured offset vector.

## Clean negatives (worth not repeating)

- **Global box-scale correction fails.** +0.006 in-sample; **-0.011 / -0.053 held out.** It was fitting noise, and the bias isn't even consistent in direction (liso2 1.33 oversized, ni_mh 0.80 undersized).
- **Temporal stacking and flat-fielding fail.** Stacking is a low-pass filter, not a denoiser: object edge SNR x0.97 -> x0.66, from 13 px residual misregistration rather than interpolation (nearest 0.59 / cubic 0.61 vs bilinear 0.55). Flat-fielding corrects a real 1.89x vignette but lowers recall. All 10 variants covered **zero** GT objects the baseline misses.

## Infrastructure

- `batterycv/evalutil.py` — one shared IoU-0.5 matcher, gated against the published ft1 result before use (`scripts/validate_harness.py`: R 0.452 vs published 0.446, AP 0.233 vs mAP50 0.252).
- Adversarially reviewed: AP@0.5 verified exact against a from-scratch reference over 4,000 curves; divergence from the original `probe_labeler.match` bounded at **+0.0019 recall**, so Phase-4 and published numbers are comparable. Six real bugs fixed, including a per-class `box/f` that was 6x low and an order-dependent `coverage()` (now optimal Hungarian matching).
- Belt physics re-verified: the ~156 px/frame figure in `lessons.md` is **correct** and BoT-SORT's rationale stands.

`probe_ensemble.py`, `probe_preprocess.py` and `probe_inference_scale.py` are built and smoke-tested but **deliberately not run to conclusions** — running them to three decimals against labels now known to be the binding error would repeat the round-1 mistake.

## Note on scope

This branch is based on `wrap-up`, so merging it also lands the two commits stranded there after PR #3 merged: the **BoT-SORT small-cell tracking fix** (`ni_cd_small` 10->49, `ni_mh_all` 12->31) and the all-runs demo index. `main` is currently missing that fix.

## Next action

**A human re-labels the 72 eval frames to a written box convention** — minimum spec: does an attached wire/connector belong inside the box (the single commonest disagreement), how are touching cells separated, how are frame-clipped objects handled. Everything else is blocked behind it.

items.title: Close the hand-search hole in the memory guards
items.body:
Retrieval is supposed to go through `cli.ts recall`, but the guards only enforced that against the Grep/Glob tools. A `grep -r` or `cat` issued through Bash bypassed both hooks: the write guard's Bash branch denies write verbs only ("Plain reads pass"), and in sessions where the Grep tool isn't exposed at all, Bash is the only path an agent has.

Guards (.claude and .codex, kept in sync by hand):
- search guard matches Bash, and denies searches/bulk reads that name a store
- ...and UNSCOPED recursive sweeps that never name it but walk into it anyway (`grep -rli "jane doe" .`, `rg jane`, `find . -name ...`) - the form hand-search actually takes in practice
- only the segment before the first pipe counts as a filesystem walk, so `git log | grep foo` passes while `grep -r ... . | head` does not
- field extraction no longer depends on one binary (jq / node). A hook that exits non-zero is a NON-BLOCKING error, so a missing dependency silently ALLOWED everything; now falls back to awk, then to raw-payload matching
- deny messages teach `recall` (agent phrasings, --complete, chain annotations) instead of the weaker `query`
- Grep/Glob no longer matches on the search pattern, so Grep(pattern="memory leak", path="src/") passes; store paths, globs, repo root and unscoped searches still deny
- .codex additionally keeps its rg --no-ignore rule (both stores are gitignored, so disabling ignore rules is a deliberate way in) and gains `recall` in its CLI allow-list, which listed only query/person/list

scripts/memory-guards.test.sh (new, runs under npm test): 63 cases pinning both the deny and allow shapes, including the no-jq path. Every hole above was found by running it, not by reading the code. All fixtures use fictional names.

.gitignore: `memory/` and `memory-graphs/` protect LOCATIONS, not CONTENT. An entry moved out of the store (scratch dir, _to_delete/, repo root) loses that protection and is one `git add .` from a public push - and an entry filename alone leaks names and topics. Added an ignore for the entry filename shape anywhere in the tree, plus _to_delete/ and _scratch/. No tracked file matches.

Routing: "pull memory" matched `pull-memories` (the Gmail/Slack ingest sweep) more closely than recall did. Narrowed that description to ingest-only and gave recall the vocabulary users actually use - pull up, recap, catch me up, brief me, prep for a 1:1. Same vocabulary added to AGENTS.md "When to act", the routing surface for agents with no skill listing. /recall's body pointed at `memory query`; corrected to `recall`.

MEMORY-GUARDRAILS.md documented only the write hook and claimed Codex has no hook layer - both wrong. It now describes both guards on both surfaces, and warns that the .claude and .codex copies are separate, have drifted before in opposite directions, and that only the .claude pair is under test.

items.title: feat(db): add SQLite as the default backend
items.body:
## Outcome

SQLite (`better-sqlite3` + Drizzle) is now the default persisted backend alongside PostgreSQL. The v1/v2 architecture gates are resolved by the authoritative v2.1 decisions, and the implementation has passed fixed-point review with no HIGH correctness findings.

Tracked by Bead `mise-en-palace-n7ip0` (closed). Base: `8d8dbea`; final reviewed head: `6de91995`.

## What changed

- Added validated `BackendKind = "sqlite" | "postgres"` configuration in `@krn/db`, with explicit flag > env > SQLite-default precedence.
- Added a complete dialect-specific SQLite schema: 51 tables / 666 columns, 63 core-owned enum checks, 115 FKs, and 213 portable indexes. PostgreSQL-only HNSW/GIN dispositions remain explicit.
- Mirrored the existing `embedding_models` and `embeddings` surfaces once; no `memory_embeddings` table or retrieval implementation. The sqlite-vec attachment point remains task 1.4.
- Added generated, package-owned SQLite migration assets and package-relative resolution; PostgreSQL migration location and identity remain unchanged.
- Added separate SQLite repositories behind existing core contracts, with dialect-neutral policy/mappers shared explicitly and no Drizzle client union.
- Persisted init now migrates and verifies the selected backend before its first registration write.
- Added SQLite candidate creation, existing review-gate promotion, and store-backed recall for the no-Postgres lifecycle proof.
- Corrected recall selection for both backends so read-model filters run before the caller's result limit. This is an intentional PostgreSQL behavior correction: it prevents a higher-ranked non-match from hiding a lower-ranked match; output templates and exit semantics are unchanged.
- Added `--backend` / `--db-path` only to existing init, doctor, migrate, and readiness shapes. No bare init or dist/build surface.
- Added truthful SQLite doctor/readiness for connectivity, exact migration identity, exact schema inventory, repository reachability, WAL, FKs, FK violations, and integrity. Unexecuted runtime proofs stay visible as `runtime_unverified` warnings.
- Narrowed `.krn` policy to regular, non-symlink, single-link `memory.db`, `memory.db-wal`, and `memory.db-shm`. Orphan sidecars, symlinks/hardlinks, Markdown/JSON, subdirectories, and all other entries fail.
- Preserved PostgreSQL output templates/ordering, exit codes, migration identity, pgvector readiness, and explicit `KRN_DATABASE_URL` behavior.
- Closed the changed-files Fallow gate without changing baselines: extracted shared DB/runtime and memory policy, reused shared mappers, scoped only intentional dialect-mirror suppressions, and fixed a missing-option parser bug plus SQLite recall handle ownership.

## Verification

- `CI=1 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — passed on Node 22.23.1.

- `pnpm typecheck` — passed across all six source packages.
- SQLite integration — persisted init migrates before registration, then candidate → production review gate → promote → recall with no PostgreSQL available.
- Real source-run SQLite init, doctor, and idempotent migrate — exit 0 with healthy store checks and explicit runtime warnings.
- PostgreSQL migrate/readiness — 61/61 identity verified, pgvector 0.8.3, source-authority integrity clean.
- PostgreSQL Drizzle schema drift gate — empty.
- Remote Linux CI: typecheck, all package tests, official MCP compatibility, CLI, doctor, changed-files Fallow, required evals, whitespace — passed.
- Remote DB readiness/smoke against disposable PostgreSQL — passed.
- Remote macOS Node 22 fast and disposable-PostgreSQL DB profiles — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Final implementation review found no HIGH correctness defect; its only MEDIUM was dependency-policy attribution, resolved below.

## Dependency-policy attribution

The dependency-policy job is red on six HIGH advisories. This was reproduced locally with the current registry and `pnpm 10.32.1` against both the detached base `8d8dbea` and head `6de91995`. Both snapshots return exactly `6 high / 8 moderate / 1 low / 0 critical`, with the same versions and dependency paths:

| `GHSA-v2hh-gcrm-f6hx` | `fast-uri@3.1.3` | `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk > ajv > fast-uri` | present | present |

items.body:
## ADR-0096 — Memory Access Model: Coordinated Hybrid

Docs-only. Decides the agent's memory-access posture (ARCH-3 from the 2026-06-26 architecture-review triage, `docs/superpowers/plans/the-following-information-comes-logical-pie.md` §4). **Status: Proposed.**

### What it decides
The external review framed it as *active retrieval-as-tool **vs** passive gateway injection* and said "pick a default." The live tree refutes the framing: **both paths are on by default and uncoordinated.** So the ADR assigns roles rather than picking one — a **coordinated hybrid**, authored measurement-first, staged in 3 phases (mirrors ADR-0094/0095):

- **Passive = ambient floor** — deterministic, gateway-owned, volatile tail (ADR-0081); fires without the brain choosing to retrieve (the FRE-502 reliability argument).
- **Active = on-demand precision** — routes through **ADR-0095**'s tool boundary + grammar-constrained digest (forward-pointer; mechanism *not* re-authored here).
- **Coordination** — de-dups the two paths, reusing `budget.py:_extract_entity_ids`.
- **D1** access-path attribution + passive↔active de-dup (no quality/money axis) · **D2** tune the default mix on data — **hard prereq FRE-593** (per-category token split) · **D3** consolidation-quality lean (research, gated).

Owner-settled forks (2026-06-26): hybrid+coordinate measure-first · FRE-593 hard prereq + 0096 adds access-path attribution · forward-pointer to ADR-0095 only.

### Codex review (codex:rescue) — 2 rounds, all findings resolved
**Round 1** (3 findings, all verified against live code & fixed):
1. *(HIGH)* Fact #1 overstated passive entity-match recall as unconditional → corrected: broad recall (`MEMORY_RECALL`) is unconditional on `is_connected()`, but entity-match recall is gated on capitalised entity hints (`context.py:194-196`).
2. *(HIGH)* Wrong tool name — `recall`, not on the allowlist → corrected to `recall_personal_history` (`sub_agent.py:97-99`), all 3 locations.
3. *(MED)* `search_memory` treated as on the discovery allowlist → corrected: it is **primary-only** (`tools/__init__.py:102`); its move behind the discovery boundary is deferred to D2.

**Round 2** (1 finding, fixed):
1. *(MED)* Division-of-labor bullet omitted the `search_memory` primary-only carve-out present in fact #6 / D2 → added the carve-out phrase for cross-section consistency.

No blocking findings remain.

items.title: docs: the core audit missed recall — measured, corrected, re-ordered
items.body:
You asked me to read the core documents for gaps and lag, and to trace the root cause **across files** instead of patching where the symptom shows. This is that pass. **No production code changed.**

## The gap was in my own audit, and it is structural

The first pass asked of every defence *"when it fires, is it right?"* and never *"does it fire at all?"* — **precision was audited, recall was not.** That is exactly why §8.1 got an `ENFORCING` verdict for a mechanism that misses most of the time, and why your session slipped through it.

| dimension | audited in pass 1 |
|---|---|
| precision — when it fires, is the decision right? | yes |
| **recall — does it fire on the inputs it exists for?** | **no** |

## Measured (§8.1)

Over the pattern file's **own** trigger phrases: 62 natural Russian phrases of 3+ words route on their own. Insert **one** neutral word (`уже` / `сейчас` / `теперь`) at a plausible position → **283 of 372 variants (76%) stop being recognised** and go to the LLM.

Six intents lose **every** variant: `autonomy_readiness`, `best_next_action`, `safe_self_check`, `source_review_plan`, `next_actions`, `project_health`.

- `«где слабое место»` routes → `«где сейчас слабое место»` does not.
- `«готов к автономной работе»` routes → `«готов уже к автономной работе»` does not.

**Root cause: one shared primitive, not 31 separate bugs.**

```python
def _has_any(text, terms): return any(term in text for term in terms)   # substring
```

Called **58 times from 31 matchers**, against **5** regexes — the five added for the capability family in #170. That PR fixed one family of thirty-one.

## Corrected (§8.11, §10 finding 3)

This document said the confidence gate was the main gap and implied making it bite. **Measured wrong.** Enforcement already exists and is wired: `core/low_evidence_policy.py` (self-described as *"the enforcement layer paired with the gate"*) + `unsupported_claims.py`, called at `core/loop.py:2170`. It is inert for three separate reasons — `mode=off` by default, the 8-chunk floor, and `no_evidence_expected` by design.

Replaying the real functions against the 8 answers recorded in `logs/` reproduced the logged verdicts **8 for 8**: flipping the mode alone changes **0** answers; a floor of 3 when `verified == 0` changes **3**. Turning the gate into a blocker would have changed **nothing** — wrong site.

## Added

- **finding 7** — the recall failure, and why a D1 failure is worse than the others: it wastes money *and* produces a wrong answer in the same turn, while everything downstream behaves correctly and cannot help;
- **finding 8** — no document here measured recall. `MASTER_ISSUE_REGISTRY` diagnoses a *missing intent kind*; the measured root is a *brittle primitive*. Fixing the former would not have changed your session: the intent kind existed and was still missed;
- **step 3b** of the verification plan — a per-intent recall proof, with its over-capture mirror in the same file, because widening recall without measuring over-capture is how a router starts hijacking ordinary questions.

## §12 re-ordered by measured damage

1. the recall failure at the primitive;
2. the memory loop banking a 0.008-confidence answer as `outcome=success` — the only one that **compounds**;
3. `_GENERATIVE_ROLES` exempting factual questions (counting TODOs is not code generation);
4. the enforcement mode and floor — dropped from first place to fourth.

## One plain gap

`docs/INDEX.md` did not list `COGNITIVE_CORE.md` at all — the newest core document was missing from the map whose job is finding documents. Added.

## Verified

`docs_link_check` ✓ · `agent_anatomy_check` (139 modules, in sync) ✓ · the three doc test suites (21 tests) ✓.

items.title: feat(11-rag): 06 Re-ranking (Cross-Encoders) — REAL two-stage pipeline over BeIR/scifact + measured nDCG/MRR
items.body:
## Second ratified RAG exemplar — built to the deepened ch04 standard (NO TOY)

Rebuilds **11 · 06 Re-ranking (Cross-Encoders)** from a toy (12 hand-made "Helios-7" passages, fake 0→1 metrics) into a **real, working, teach-live-able** chapter over a labelled IR benchmark, matching the deepened ch04 on every axis.

### What's real now
- **Benchmark:** **BeIR/scifact** — 5,183 real scientific abstracts, 300 real test queries, **real human relevance judgments (qrels)** — so every metric is grounded in truth.
- **Stage 1:** real bi-encoder **all-MiniLM-L6-v2**, exact cosine top-K via numpy `argpartition` (no faiss → dodges the torch/faiss OpenMP conflict).
- **Stage 2:** real cross-encoder **ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2**, joint `[CLS] q [SEP] d` scoring, re-sort by logit.
- **Measured over all 300 queries:** **nDCG@10 0.648 → 0.687**, **MRR@10 0.607 → 0.656**, Recall@10 0.788 → 0.809, and **Recall@100 0.925 → 0.925 (INVARIANT)** — the recall ceiling *proven by measurement*, not asserted from a toy. Real latency: retrieve **0.37 ms** vs rerank top-100 **1102 ms** (~2,978×). Real quality-vs-K sweep (knee at K≈5). Device-agnostic (cuda→mps→cpu; this run on `mps`).

### The honest, corrected recall-ceiling story
Reranking **raises** Recall@10 (it promotes in-pool gold from ranks 11–100 into the top-10) but **cannot change Recall@K over the whole pool** — that flat 0.925→0.925 is the true ceiling. The module *asserts* pool-recall invariance before printing.

### Math derived in full (with provenance)
Bi-encoder factorized dot-product vs cross-encoder joint cross-attention (why the factorization structurally can't model term interaction, and the accuracy/cost consequence); the two-stage cost model; DCG→nDCG and MRR derivations + the Recall@k-vs-Recall@pool distinction; **ColBERT MaxSim** ($\sum_i\max_j \mathbf q_i\cdot\mathbf d_j$) and **MonoT5** (relevance = softmax over "true"/"false") as the interaction/cost middle grounds. Every formula carries a bold Source/derivation line; every source is in `.references.md`.

### Deliverables
- Rewritten note `.md` (full gold flow; the note **explains the code** — retrieval, pair-scoring, the K-sweep, the metric computation — in prose).
- `.references.md` (+ scifact + model cards + MonoT5; ≥4 videos, arXiv ids).
- `code/reranking.py` — typed real module, from-scratch metrics (multi-gold), cached embeddings.
- `code/build_notebook.py` → the **12-step** teaching notebook; **executes headless, 0 errors**, real outputs (incl. a real hero query: a buried gold rescued from rank #11 → #1).
- `code/make_figures_06.py` → **7 figures** — 5 real-measured (ndcg_mrr, quality_vs_k, latency_vs_k, score_separation, rank_shuffle) + 2 schematic (funnel, bi_vs_cross). Embedding/ordering caches gitignored.

### Honesty
The lift is real but **modest** (+0.038 nDCG) because all-MiniLM is already a strong first stage — stated plainly as the honest lesson (a reranker is a *measurable* upgrade, not free magic). All page numbers trace to the executed `reranking.py` run (summary.json); figures regenerate from the same run; recall is deterministic, latency reported as medians. ruff clean; notebook 0 errors.

1. **The GSV-tier confound is resolved.** With paterson pooled, the GSV tier's F1-optimum moved **0.50 → 0.26**, into the cluster with every other tier (0.26–0.35). bend's outlier was in-domain-ness, not GSV. Per-tier thresholds remain unjustified — the case is now stronger.

items.title: fix(delta): scorers must prove they measured what they were given
items.body:
Three defects, one shape: a scorer reported a plausible number without checking it had actually measured its input. Two were found by the `sizemax` audit and the v3.0.1 Delta runs (jobs 20675479 / 20675480).

## 1. Recall denominators were never checked against the truth

truvari's `TP-base + FN` is a **post-filter** count. When a filter discards truth records, recall is computed over a subset and nothing says so. The audit found **4 such cases in 152 per-type checks** (job_19758751 DEL reported 0.800 where the full denominator gives 0.727; job_20636298 INV 0.800 vs 0.667).

`check_denominator` compares the scorer's base count against the truth handed to it, checking the **outcome** rather than enumerating causes so it generalises past `--sizemax`. On a mismatch it prints the corrected recall and attributes the loss exactly, by differencing the truth against truvari's own `tp-base`/`fn` output.

**This also closed a hole in Rule 0.** A filter drops a record from base *and* comparison alike, so truth-vs-truth still scores a perfect **1.000** over the surviving subset — the selftest could only ever catch a *total* drop, never a partial one.

## 2. BND span derivation never ran, and reported that as a fact about the data

`build_bnd_spans` was **called at line 264 and defined at line 514**. Bash resolves function names at call time, so every run hit `command not found` (127), and the call site's `|| echo "(BND span derivation produced nothing — no intra-contig junctions?)"` turned exit 127 into a plausible statement about the data. On a single-contig reference, where every junction is necessarily intra-contig, that explanation was not merely wrong but impossible.

So the BNDspan path — the mechanism that recovers a caller which re-represents a junction, and the entire reason the derivation exists — **has never executed**. `manta_BND recall=0.000` in job 20675480 was measured with the only thing that could have matched it absent, and Manta emits inversions as breakend pairs (`manta_INV: caller emitted no INV records`), so it is the case that most needed it.

A second, independent silent failure sat underneath: the body writes `END=` but only `SVLEN` was backfilled, so an undeclared `END` parses as `Type=String` and `bcftools sort` dies — hidden by `2>/dev/null`, after which the function **returned 0 having written nothing**. It now inherits the source header and backfills only what is missing, surfaces sort's stderr, and verifies the written record count equals the junction count it derived.

Exit status is three-way, because "no spans" has two unrelated meanings: `0` written, `2` all junctions inter-contig (legitimate), `1` anything else. The caller handles each with an explicit `*)` arm.

## 3. #457's query filtering missed the two runs that needed it

Per-type runs filtered the query; the aggregate and BND runs passed the whole call set, so truvari counted every record of an excluded type as a false positive:

- job 20675480: `manta_BND FP=43` against `manta_overall FP=24`. **A subset cannot have more false positives than the whole** — the same arithmetic impossibility #457 was opened for.
- The aggregate truth excludes BND/CNV by construction, so the query now does too (via `-e`, so a record with no `SVTYPE` is kept rather than silently dropped), and logs what it set aside.
- The BND run compares breakends to breakends, so its query is now the caller's BND records only.

`BNDspan`'s query stays unfiltered **by design** — the caller may use any `SVTYPE` for a junction — which makes recall the measurement and precision/FP/f1 uninterpretable there. The output now says so rather than leaving the number to be quoted.

## 4. VAF coverage is enforced, not warned about

Job 20675479 **confirms the #450 fix on real data**: three clusters in the per-decile table where there were two, 543 of 567 planted sites scored where 407 were. But the harness still could not notice its own failure mode — `only-truth=24` was a one-line stderr warning, and localising those 24 meant differencing two tables by hand.

The metrics cannot be the coverage gate, because dropping the lowest-VAF stratum makes them look **better**:

| | bias | MAE | r | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| complete set | +0.0008 | 0.0240 | 0.9846 | PASS |
| #450 (lowest cluster excluded) | **+0.0011** | **0.0227** | **0.9803** | PASS ← |

Both pass every threshold; only the denominator separates them. `scn_af_compare.py` now prints planted/scored/unscored per decile and exits non-zero above `--max-uncovered-frac` (default 10%). Every planted bin prints even when nothing in it survived — `if bd:` meant an excluded stratum *vanished from the table*, and a missing row is far harder to spot than `0 of 104 — NOTHING SCORED`.

## Failure handling

Both pipelines previously exited **before** `archive_run`, discarding the artifacts most worth keeping. Failures are now deferred past archiving: every discrepancy is reported inline next to the comparison it affects, artifacts are archived, and only then does the job exit non-zero. The SV summary banner no longer prints an unqualified `complete` over a run whose numbers are unusable.

## Evidence

All local, driving the **real** functions extracted from the scripts rather than copies:

- Denominator check: at `--sizemax 5000000` on a 5-record truth with one 20 Mb DEL, pre-change output is `recall=1.000 TP=4` and `selftest: PASS` — **both look correct**; the check fires in both places and names the discarded record. At an adequate `sizemax` it is completely silent.
- Forward-reference failure reproduced in isolation: exit 127 swallowed by the `||` branch, script exits 0.
- `build_bnd_spans` across all three paths (intra+inter / all-inter / unparsable ALT) → `0`/`2`/`1`, writing exactly the 2 expected spans — on a fixture that does **not** declare `END`, i.e. the case that previously failed silently.
- VAF gate on fixtures reproducing job 20675479's architecture: passes at the observed 4.2% shortfall and localises it per stratum; fails with the zero row when the lowest cluster is excluded. Driving the real gate block with #450's `compare.txt` gives PASS at `rc=0` and FAIL at `rc=1` on **identical** bias/MAE.
- `set -e` interactions checked rather than assumed: a short-circuited `[[ … ]] && cmd` does not abort, and `cmd | tee || rc=$?` captures the status without aborting.

## Status

**In progress, not done.** Locally vetted; **not yet exercised against real truvari on Delta** (not installed on this workstation).

Specifically **NOT verified**: that truvari with `-t` actually matches a derived `<BND_SPAN>` to a caller's `<DUP:TANDEM>` at the same coordinates. That is the prediction the next `sv_pipeline.sbatch` run tests, and it is the one that decides whether BND recall was ever a real result.

CHANGELOG also corrected: the v3.0.1 entry asserted truvari "cannot match" a breakend and credited a `bnd_proximity.py` that was never committed. `--bnddist` has existed since truvari v5.0.0; Delta runs v5.4.0.

- preserve per-film failure isolation and all identity safeguards

items.title: fix(search): bound cross-encoder relevance to [0,1] + resolve journal-quartile abbreviations
items.body:
## What changed

Post-Phase-1 ranking fixes that protect trial-primary papers and landmark RCTs, lifting throttle-corrected recall@10 from **0.716 → 0.90** on the 87q harness with **no unit regressions**.

- **Bound the cross-encoder relevance to `[0,1]`** (`cca0f662`). The MedCPT Cross-Encoder emits raw logits (~ -16..+10). Fed un-normalized into the quality composite at weight 0.40, a single negative logit on a trial's PRIMARY report drove the composite to ~ -2.8 and buried the canonical answer beneath acronym-mentioning secondaries. Fix: sigmoid-squash the logit at the reranker adapter so `rerankScore` is one *capped* signal (weight 0.30) in a metadata-dominant composite. **Drops the dead LangSearch tier** (500s for this account; wrong infra fallback). Chain is now MedCPT -> Cohere -> fail-open to metadata/keyword order.
- **Resolve ISO journal abbreviations to Scimago quartiles** (`90e4c2f5`). PubMed returns `N Engl J Med`/`J Am Coll Cardiol`, which aren't substrings of Scimago's full-name keys, so landmark NEJM/JACC papers got the unknown-journal quartile (0.1) instead of Q1 (1.0). Adds a positional token-prefix abbreviation matcher + an empty-journal guard.
- **Docs** (`663f6f18`): PHASE-01-STATUS floor-close evidence + ARCHITECTURE rerank refresh.

The earlier "recall 0.716 < floor 0.88" was mis-attributed to a query-planning lacuna. Root cause was these two ranking bugs. The cross-encoder is now net-additive (0.85 > metadata-only 0.82 > raw-rerank 0.716).

items.title: feat(ingestion): Java large-repo LSP augmentation — readiness + coverage + pre-filter (ADR-002 P0/P1)
items.body:
## Summary
Implements ADR-002 Phase 0 + the feasible part of Phase 1 — the **correctness + honesty floor** for LSP augmentation on large Java repos. Three work-streams:
- **WS-A — jdtls settle-until-quiet readiness.** Replaces the premature `language/status ServiceReady` gate (fires ~3.5s, before Maven/classpath indexing completes ~19s) with a settle-until-quiet model: ready when `$/progress` has been silent for `JDTLS_QUIET_INTERVAL_MS` AND a self-rescheduling canary resolves, with a `JDTLS_READY_DEADLINE_MS` backstop. Adds `JAVA_ADAPTER.clientCapabilities {window:{workDoneProgress:true}}` (fresh literal; Java leaves the TS byte-identical-capability set). `language/status` ServiceReady is consume-and-ignore.
- **WS-B — coverage honesty.** Adds `probed` + `preFilteredExternal` counters to `ReconciliationReport` (accumulated in `withReconciliationSession`, threaded via the work-fn payload), a `--lsp-budget <n>` CLI flag (commander; `Number.isInteger && >0`), and extends the funnel line in-place with `(budget B of N candidates)`, emitted on all paths (success, dry-run, gate-failure, error). No more silent under-augmentation.
- **WS-C — correction-candidate external pre-filter.** A `canSkipCandidate` seam skips correction candidates whose `oldTargetId` resolves to an external-zone graph node, before dispatch. Pre-filtered candidates route to an external-refusal sentinel so the replay does not corrupt confirmed/corrected/recall/refused.

## Scope boundary (honest)
**The ~57k recall-probe waste on Spring services is NOT addressed by this PR.** Recall candidates carry the *caller's* call-site file, not the callee's location, and no callee→external-import binding — so they cannot be pre-filtered without threading FQN bindings (`java.`/`javax.`/`jakarta.`/dep-pkg) from the call-processor into the recall feed. items.title: fix(cradle): correct specificity-mislabeled-as-precision (governance metric)
items.body:
## (c) Governance correction — the part that matters (read first)
The crisis-precision sign-off thread (`docs/superpowers/governance/2026-06-14-crisis-precision-s3-signoff-package.md`) reasons about the **false-positive / over-triage** metric, i.e. **precision** (of everything flagged crisis, how much was real). The CRADLE figure circulating as "precision ≈95.7%" is actually **specificity** (TN/(TN+FP) = 178/186). **True precision = TP/(TP+FP) = 86/94 = 91.5%** — so roughly **1 in 12 crisis flags is a false positive, not 1 in 23**.

**Changes no decision:** #18 already ruled out the S1/S3 precision fix as recall-unsafe; S2/MARBERT stays the convergent answer for both the FP burden and the ~37% recall. The slightly larger FP burden **strengthens** the case for S2, never weakens it. This corrects a number safety reasoning rests on — please route for the same clinical/owner awareness as the rest of that package.

## Scope of the correction (honest bounds)
Denominators (verified against `eval.jsonl`: 232 crisis / 186 safe / 182 clinical = 600), formulas, and arithmetic were re-checked. The **numerators (TP=86, FP=8, TN=178) are taken from the frozen 2026-06-05 baseline and were NOT re-derived** by re-running `safety_check` over the 232 cases. The claim is exactly: *"the 95.7% figure is mislabeled; given the frozen numerators, true precision is 91.5%."* This is **not** a re-validation of the classifier — if TP is itself off, 91.5% moves with it.

## What's correct vs corrected
- **Recall = 37.1% (86/232): always correct.** Gating KPI and pilot NO-GO unaffected.
- **"Precision 95.7%": was specificity.** True precision 91.5% (86/94), computed for the first time.

## (a) Structural fix — the durable one
`conftest.py` computed `TN/(TN+FP)` into a variable misnamed `precision` and printed it (correctly) as "Specificity"; downstream docs inherited the variable name. Now the summary computes `tp`/`fp` **once from the same run** and prints **Recall TP/(TP+FN)**, **Precision TP/(TP+FP)**, and **Specificity TN/(TN+FP)**, each with its formula. An unlabeled number can't be inherited and renamed wrong again. Verified: same-run `tp`/`fp`, no re-pull.

## (b) Doc label corrections
- `tests/test_cradle_bench.py` header: PRECISION→SPECIFICITY, added true precision + correction note + caveat.

items.title: fix(memory): reconcile search must be patient — 2s fail-open silently degraded corrections to ADD
items.body:
Live Telegram-lane test of the supersession chain (demo user, exactly as the bridge calls `/api/chat`) found corrections **stacking instead of superseding** whenever the correction arrives while the box is busy — i.e. the realistic case, since the embedder is still working the turn.

items.body:
Turns the corpus-mining loop into shipped, tested artifacts — and hardens the dispatcher that is, as of this PR, running our first fully-own-data adapter train.

**Two pre-registered, refute-then-corrected experiments** (the honest record is pinned by tests so it can't be laundered):
- **`looped_recall_input_dependence.py`** (+4 tests) — grounds [arXiv:2604.15259](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15259). Pre-registered H1 (input-independence collapse) was **refuted by the run**: the no-recall failure is *non-reachability* (conv=0 for ρ≤1.5). Corrected claim reproduced: recall + outer normalization → reachable, input-dependent fixed points at every ρ (even expansive ρ=3). Reading: **recall = per-step grounding**; no-recall ill-posedness is the well-posedness analogue of cert §2 collapse.
- **`calibration_to_profit_edge.py`** — grounds [arXiv:2607.00164](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00164) + the profit-on-prediction-markets literature. H2's magnitude was **refuted honestly**: the bias+Kelly edge (+0.0009/event) barely clears the no-edge noise floor (+0.0007) and turns negative with modest forecast error. Reproduces "calibration ≠ profit": the dominant lever is *having a large real information edge*, not calibration or sizing.

**`modal_dispatch.py` hardening**: `_run_logged` subprocess capture (the first E-B dispatches died with an opaque signal-6 because output wasn't captured — never again), `--repo-ref` branch dispatch (train from a branch pre-merge), `memory=32GiB` worker RAM.

**`data/eval/distill-replay.jsonl`** (2,600 records, distill + Tulu-3 anchor, decontaminated) committed for E-B arm B — completes what #2719 started.

items.title: feat(memory): selective corrective retrieval (CRAG) on high-stakes recall
items.body:
## What & why

Genesis was expected to have CRAG (corrective retrieval) wired; only the calibrated
rubric existed. **W-CRAG v1** closes that: when an explicit `memory_recall` /
`knowledge_recall` returns clearly off-topic results, Genesis grades them and
self-corrects — broadening the search, drawing on the knowledge base (and, for
knowledge queries, the web) — instead of feeding itself junk context. Follows
canonical CRAG (arXiv 2401.15884): lightweight evaluator → confidence → 3-bucket policy.

## Design (decisions locked with the user)

- **Grader:** new `crag_grade` call site (fast cross-vendor: `openrouter-haiku` →
  free fallbacks), reusing a new `memory_recall_grounding_runtime` rubric variant
  (the calibrated relevance rubric, minus the eval-only `{expected}` placeholder so
  runtime traces don't pollute eval calibration). Added to degradation skip sets.
- **Conservative rollout:** latency pre-gate (skip grading when the top score is
  already confident); **ACT only on a clear `Incorrect` verdict** (relaxed
  re-retrieve + raw KB; **web fallback on the knowledge path only** — episodic
  memory isn't on the web); **`Ambiguous` is DARK** (logged, no action) so the
  grader's thresholds can be calibrated on real traffic before widening.
- **Best-effort & latency-safe:** per-grade `asyncio.wait_for` timeout + graceful
  pass-through on any failure → a working recall is never degraded or stalled, even
  if the grader is down. Augmentation uses the **raw retriever** (no self-nesting).
- **Wiring:** default-ON on `memory_recall` (non-compact path) + `knowledge_recall`.
  Latency-sensitive paths (proactive hook, voice, CC context injection, ego) use the
  raw retriever and are **unaffected**. `emit_recall_corrected` logs every decision
  for calibration.

## Verification

- ruff clean; **139 tests pass** — 21 new `test_corrective.py` unit tests + regression
  across `test_mcp/test_memory_mcp`, `test_memory/test_mcp_integration`,
  `test_dashboard/test_tool_api`, `test_eval/*` (no regressions).
- **E2E against the real grader** (`openrouter-haiku`): relevant memory → score **1.0**
  → Correct (kept, no augmentation); irrelevant → **0.0** → Incorrect → augmentation
  fires (`relaxed` + raw `source=knowledge`), no web on the memory path; calibration
  `recall_corrected` events written; grader-unavailable → graceful pass-through.
- Architecture-reviewed pre-build (8 risks folded in) and code-reviewed post-build
  (Codex quota-exhausted → Claude code-reviewer; 2 findings fixed: web-result shape,
  knowledge-path event linkage).

## Out of scope (deferred follow-ups)

- Widen `Ambiguous` → acting once logged calibration data validates the thresholds.
- Corrective on the **compact** recall path (compact returns truncated previews — no
  gradeable content; callers expand later).
- Episodic strip-refinement / LLM-graded web chunks; post-deploy grader calibration review.

## ⚠️ DO NOT MERGE YET

Holding merge — multiple concurrent sessions are working on closely related
memory/routing systems. Merge only after coordination.

- **76–97% of sink failures had complete gold evidence within the top-5 sessions fed to gen** — pure synthesis failure, not retrieval.
- **temporal-reasoning (79 failures):** dominated by confident wrong temporal grounding (44 hallucinated-fact, 37 with full evidence in context) + 11 explicit arithmetic errors; the model has the dates and fails to anchor/compute.

items.body:
## Bug

`endSessionAction` (`apps/web/src/lib/session/actions.ts`) dispatches the session-start-probe
outcome to the between-session/booster scheduler (`onSessionStartOutcome` / `onBoosterOutcome`,
dispatch-by-mode fixed in #27). It read the raw first trial's outcome (`snapshot.trials[0].outcome`).

Per PLAN §4.2 v4, **two consecutive unclears on a probe confirm a miss**. But
`handleStartProbe` in the engine (`packages/core/src/sr/session.ts`) still records that
*terminal* trial with `outcome: "unclear"` (and `corrected: true`) — it preserves the literal
caregiver tap, it doesn't relabel it. `trials[0]` is also the wrong index in this case: it's the
first, *non-terminal* unclear (`corrected: false`); the resolving trial is later in the array.

Both `onSessionStartOutcome` and `onBoosterOutcome` treat `outcome === "unclear"` as an
intentional no-op (correct — an unresolved unclear must not move the schedule). The net effect:
a genuine start-of-session miss reached via double-unclear never shrank the between-session gap
or dropped the booster step, in **both** modes.

## Fix

Added a small pure helper, `resolvedStartProbeOutcome(trials)`, to `packages/core/src/sr/session.ts`
(exported via the existing `export * from "./session"` in `packages/core/src/sr/index.ts` — no new
export wiring needed). It scans the trial log from the front, skips still-open re-probes
(`unclear` + `corrected: false`), and returns the first trial that actually terminates the start
probe:

- `recall` (always `corrected: false` for a real start-probe recall) → `"recall"`
- `miss` (always `corrected: true`) → `"miss"`
- `unclear` + `corrected: true` (the double-unclear conversion) → resolves to `"miss"`
- anything else (e.g. the guaranteed 0s end-of-session win after a caregiver closes mid re-probe)
  → `null`, meaning the start probe was never actually resolved — same no-op as before

`endSessionAction` now dispatches this resolved outcome instead of the raw `trials[0]` read, still
gated by mode (`existing.mode === "booster"` → `onBoosterOutcome`, else `onSessionStartOutcome`) per
#27. `unclear`-never-moves-the-ladder semantics inside `session.ts`'s reducer are untouched — this
is purely about correctly classifying what the resolved start probe outcome *was* for the
scheduler, not about changing the engine's within-session unclear handling.

Fixed in **core** (new helper) + **app** (call site swap), because the resolution rule is an
engine-level fact about how a double-unclear collapses to a miss — it belongs next to
`handleStartProbe`/`startProbeMiss`, not re-derived in the web layer.

### Related (not in scope here)

`packages/core/src/sim/simulate.ts`'s `driveSession` tracks its own `startProbeOutcome` from the
raw per-probe draw, with the same blind spot (it also ends up "unclear" instead of "miss" on a
double-unclear start probe fed into the simulated scheduler calls). Left untouched since it's a
separate call site or the population simulator, not the `endSessionAction` path this bug report
was about — flagging in case it's worth a follow-up.

## Tests

**Core** (`packages/core/src/sr/session.test.ts`) — 5 new unit tests for
`resolvedStartProbeOutcome`: direct recall, direct miss, double-unclear → `"miss"`, a single
still-open unclear → `null`, empty trials → `null`.

**Web** (`apps/web/src/lib/session/actions.test.ts`) — 3 new regression tests on
`endSessionAction`, reusing the existing chainable Supabase stub harness:
- (e) existing BETWEEN schedule + double-unclear start-probe miss → `onSessionStartOutcome` shrinks
  the gap (was a no-op before the fix)
- (e2) existing BOOSTER schedule + double-unclear start-probe miss → `onBoosterOutcome` drops the
  step (was a no-op before the fix)
- (f) a single still-open (non-terminal) unclear stays a true no-op (regression guard against
  over-fixing)

items.body:
## Recall-Aware Robustness Re-analysis (RARR) — design spec + Plan 8a

First of a 5-plan roadmap (8a–8e). Plans 8b–8e continue on this branch.

**Design:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-22-recall-aware-robustness-reanalysis-design.md` (Rev 2). Keeps the kappa-concordance question/statistic primary; adds hierarchical pooling, recall-corrected ranking, and Plackett-Luce as declared robustness specs; fixes the recall-calibration foundation; pre-registers anti-gaming controls; RunPod compute policy (GPU for the classifier bake-off, CPU for the Bayesian fits).

### Plan 8a changes (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-22-plan8a-engine-correctness-foundations.md`)
1. **Recall from gold truth-vs-prediction** — recall posteriors derive solely from the adjudicated goldset (per-entry truth-cell denominators); sparse entries get honest wide posteriors instead of falsely-precise `Beta(1,101)`.
2. **Manifest schema-versioning** — `goldset_hash` added additively; v1 canonical form is byte-stable so the frozen 2026 lock is unaffected.
3. **Provenance binding** — reproduction bundle records `goldset_hash`; calibrate provenance hashes the classifier label file.
4. **Incidence ranking** — concordance ranks by incidence `λ·size` (multi-stratum sum), not bare latent λ.
5. **Live overlap `W`** — built from the goldset confusion matrix, activating the precision/false-positive term (previously inert); fails loud if a present goldset can't load.
6. **Robustness wiring** — `run_robustness_inference` wired into infer→decide→report behind a completeness gate; `SpecResult` extended for heterogeneous outputs (σ_u, alternate rankings).

### Verification
Local: ruff, mypy (97 files), pytest (full suite with viz extras), semgrep (0 findings), two-cycle parity proof — all green. Each task passed an independent spec+quality review; the final whole-branch review caught and fixed a repo-wide ruff gate violation and a latent `KeyError` on sparse data.

items.title: fix(memory): honest recall — real embedder for semantics, HRR is lexical
items.body:
## Why

A live demo of the memory store caught an overclaim: **HRR bag-of-words recall is not semantic.** A paraphrased, keyword-free query ("when does the accounting period begin") matched the *wrong* fact. An empirical sweep confirmed it — 1/5 correct, and only where a literal token overlapped. The earlier "keyword-free semantic recall" unit test passed by coincidence (2 candidates). HRR ranks by cosine over a token hash: that's **lexical/associative**, not trained meaning.

## Fix (honest, not cosmetic)

- **`PgMemory` takes an optional `embedder`** (any `BaseEmbedding`, e.g. brokered OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`). With one, recall is **true semantic** and the vector column follows the embedder's dimension. Without one it falls back to the HRR `[cos φ, sin φ]` encoding (offline, lexical) — the zero-infra OSS default.
- **`capabilities.semantic_search` now tells the truth**: `True` only with a real embedder; `HolographicStore` reports `False` (it supports `search`, not semantic recall).
- **Docstrings say it plainly**: HRR = lexical/associative; embedder = semantic. Pick the embedder to match how much recall quality is worth.
- **Tests corrected**: coincidental "keyword-free" assertions become robust shared-token associative recall; a **new integration test proves real paraphrase recall with a live embedder** ("accounting period" → the fiscal-year fact; "drink" → coffee), gated on `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

## Proof

- Unit gate green: 4955 passed, 96.83%.
- Integration **7/7 against real Postgres** (local + CI pgvector), incl. the real-embedder semantic test.
- Live demo now recalls correctly with the embedder; RLS isolation + untrusted-scrubbed injection unchanged.

Follows #43. This is the open-core split done honestly: HRR offline default, real embeddings for the enterprise tier.

items.title: fix(attendance): the register opened on the browser's UTC day, not the school's
items.body:
Reviewed the attendance page for the ambiguity found on the scan, meetings, HR and finance pages. **Two of the three things I most expected to be wrong were already right** — recorded below — and the defect was in the one place nobody looks, because it's prefilled and looks correct.

```ts
const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
```

That's the **UTC** date. The API decides the term lock and the 7-day stale rule in the **school's** zone, so the page and the server disagreed about what day it is:

```
Africa/Lagos     23:30 local → UTC says 06 Aug, the school 07 Aug
America/Toronto  22:30 local → UTC says 06 Aug, the school 05 Aug
Asia/Singapore   01:00 local → UTC says 06 Aug, the school 07 Aug
```

A teacher west of UTC taking an evening register filed it against **yesterday**; one east of UTC in the early morning filed **tomorrow**. The field is prefilled, so there's no moment at which anybody would think to check.

Now derived from the school's timezone, which rides the session — so the server render and the client render agree. Deriving it from the runtime is the hydration mismatch CLAUDE.md warns about. **One** memoised value feeds the default, the picker's `max` and the Today button, so those three can't drift apart.

## Second finding

Same shape as the meetings announce: saving a register messages the guardians of everyone marked absent or late, and the page said so **afterwards** (*"Guardians were notified"*). It now says so **before**, with the count — a mis-tick corrected later doesn't recall the message.

## What I checked and found sound

- a >7-day edit does **not** report "Saved". It says the change went for approval, names who can approve it, and points at Approvals — the silent-success failure this review was looking for is already handled
- only pupils with **no existing record** default to PRESENT; existing marks prefill, so Save can't silently mark a whole class present
- the term lock is consulted **before** the register is filled in and disables the board, rather than being discovered on save after the work is done

Web production build; route smoke for teacher, school_admin and parent; timezone arithmetic verified against three real zones. Web-only, no API change.
